clues: A judicial officer empowered under Nigerian statute to investigate unnatural deaths.
Holds authority to order a medico-legal autopsy or exhumation of a buried body.
Presides over an inquest to establish the identity of the deceased and how, when, and where death occurred.
A fact-finding judicial inquiry rather than a criminal trial to convict an offender.
Mandatorily convened when a person dies in police custody or prison.
Formal legal inquiry presided over by a Coroner into a sudden, violent, or unexplained death.

terms.sub: Diagnosis of Death and Brain Death
clues: Confirmed clinically by testing cranial nerve reflexes and medullary response to hypercarbia.
Requires prior exclusion of hypothermia, sedative drugs, and metabolic coma.
Irreversible cessation of all functions of the brainstem, constituting legal death even while ventilated.
An early post-mortem sign useful for estimating time since death within the first 24 hours.
Influenced by ambient temperature, clothing, body mass, and air movement.
Post-mortem cooling of the corpse until it reaches environmental temperature.
Becomes fixed after 8 to 12 hours and helps indicate whether a body was moved.
Appears bright cherry-red in carbon monoxide poisoning.
Purplish-red gravitational settling of blood in dependent capillaries after circulation stops, also called hypostasis.
A rare forensic phenomenon associated with extreme emotional or physical stress at death.
May leave a suicide victim tightly gripping a firearm or a drowning victim clutching river weeds.
Instantaneous stiffening of active voluntary muscles at the exact moment of death without primary flaccidity.
Driven largely by endogenous anaerobic bacteria such as Clostridium perfringens.
First appears externally as greenish discoloration over the right iliac fossa.
Late post-mortem bacterial decomposition and liquefaction of body tissues with foul-smelling gas.
A modified late post-mortem change seen in bodies submerged in water or buried in damp graves.
Preserves external body contours and injuries for months or years.
Greasy, yellowish-white, soap-like substance formed by hydrolysis and hydrogenation of body fats.
Requires a formal legal order from a Coroner or court before it can be performed.
Mandates collection of surrounding control soil samples when poisoning is suspected.
Lawful digging up and removal of an already buried corpse from its grave for medico-legal examination.
